text.title: Outcome Based Roadmaps Advanced Core Rules
text.summary: 10 testable rules every Outcome Based Roadmaps Advanced application must enforce — r1-r5 govern the multi-quarter chain, r6-r10 govern goal decomposition and multi-audience emission. These are HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Roadmap MUST link outcomes across quarters via explicit edges; floating per-quarter outcomes are rejected.
rule.rationale: Cross-quarter chains expose dependency surprises early.

rule.statement: Every dependency edge MUST carry type {hard, soft} + rationale; un-typed edges are rejected.
Confidence MUST follow decay model (Q+1 high, Q+2 medium, Q+3+ low) unless cited evidence justifies higher; over-confident long-horizon items are rejected.
rule.rationale: Confidence-decay matches empirical accuracy; over-confidence rooms accumulate planning debt.

rule.statement: Roadmap MUST have one swim lane per product (≥2); single-lane roadmaps reduce to base methodology.
rule.rationale: Swim lanes prevent products competing inside one outcome.

rule.statement: Each quarter's review MUST update the multi-quarter chain (which edges shifted, which decayed); roadmap-without-review is rejected.
rule.rationale: Without iterative review the multi-quarter chain ossifies and stops representing reality.

rule.statement: The horizon MUST be anchored to a business goal falsifiable on a date — metric, current value, target, deadline. That deadline is the only exact date permitted anywhere in the artefact; every other horizon expression stays a confidence label per r3.
rule.rationale: A multi-quarter chain with no falsifiable root is unreviewable: nothing at quarter close can be shown to have failed, so r5 degrades into a status update.

rule.statement: Every product outcome MUST carry a one-sentence causal hypothesis linking it upward to the business goal; an outcome that cannot state how it moves the goal is rejected.
rule.rationale: Dependency edges say what must precede what; the causal hypothesis says why any of it is worth doing, and without it a well-typed chain can still be pointed at nothing.

rule.statement: Every outcome MUST carry exactly one leading indicator readable weekly — not only at quarter close. More than one indicator per outcome is rejected as ambiguity about what is being steered.
rule.rationale: On a multi-quarter horizon a quarter-end-only metric gives at most four reads per year, which is too coarse to correct a chain before its later quarters are already committed.

rule.statement: Every experiment MUST have success criteria written before it starts, and MUST be tagged with the outcome id it serves; criteria authored after results are read are rejected.
rule.rationale: Criteria written after the fact are fitted to whatever happened, which converts an experiment into a justification and lets confidence rise on no evidence — the exact input r3 decays.

rule.statement: The customer, board, engineering and sales views MUST be rendered from one source tree; a per-audience artefact edited by hand is rejected.
rule.rationale: Hand-maintained audience copies diverge within a quarter, and the divergence is discovered in the room where the two audiences meet.
